mainText:
The Ipsos poll shows Labour extending its lead over National on almost every major election issue, with election day Saturday the seventh of November.

New Zealand.

A new Ipsos poll has Labour trusted to manage sixteen of twenty measured issues better than National, including fuel prices, which has climbed into the top three voter concerns. The campaign's final week has turned bitter. Don Brash has accused Christopher Luxon of misleading the public over vote splitting tactics, after National, ACT and New Zealand First clashed over a Reality Check Radio advertising campaign Brash wrote himself. ACT's Paul Henry separately called National two faced over the issue. Green co leader Chlöe Swarbrick says she has faced repeated attacks after National claimed she would be finance minister in a change of government.

Police say officer issued speeding offences in Western Bay of Plenty surged five hundred and twenty five percent between 2021 and 2025, from two thousand six hundred and fifty two offences to sixteen thousand five hundred and seventy nine. Rotorua's Eastgate intersection has been granted three point four six million dollars in government funding for new traffic lights, after years of safety concerns at the Business Park site.

A review has found police could possibly have prevented the murders of Fuk-Fu Joseph Kwok and his wife Mei Han Chong, after a double murderer obtained their address through the Disputes Tribunal despite objections. The review calls the tribunal's release of the address a significant factor in the killings.

One person is critically injured after a single vehicle crash on Te Pua Road and Lake Road in Kaikohe, just before seven a.m. yesterday. Emergency services remain at the scene.

A new front is moving up the country, bringing heavy rain to the west and northwest gales to the south and east. Separately, police warned league fans after convoys of vehicles backing Samoa and Tonga blocked intersections in Tauranga, with infringement notices issued for noise and obstruction.

World.

Rwanda backed rebels have entered Goma, a safe haven city in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with residents reporting gunfire and shelling after Congolese troops were overrun. United Nations officials estimate more than one million displaced people are now inside the city, with no clear resolution date.

Israel has allowed displaced Gazans to begin crossing a military zone that bisects the enclave on foot, after a deadlock over hostage releases was broken. It follows the release of four more female Israeli hostages under the ceasefire deal. Some of the freed women still had shrapnel in their bodies from the October 2007 attack, according to an Israeli medical official, and had spent up to eight months in tunnels.

Protests over the cost of living turned violent in Germany, with looting reported in Frankfurt, Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg after largely peaceful daytime demonstrations. Similar protests also drew hundreds of thousands in France. In France separately, prosecutors have opened an attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb attacks injured security officers during Saturday's protests.

Technology.

Binance is attempting to recover six point three billion US dollars stolen in a hack it describes as the largest of its kind on record. Two analytics firms have linked the attack to a North Korean hacking unit known as TraderTraitor, and the FBI says North Korea was responsible. Binance says it has covered ninety percent of customer losses from its own funds, with the recovery effort continuing.

Alphabet, Google's parent company, has lost about five hundred billion US dollars in market value after revealing its own artificial intelligence search summaries are cutting into advertising revenue. The stock hit a six month low. It is part of a broader sell off, with the Nasdaq at its lowest level in more than two months, as investors question whether nearly one trillion US dollars in artificial intelligence spending is matched by returns.

Sport.

Formula One. Liam Lawson has been disqualified from qualifying for the Mexican Grand Prix over a power rules breach and starts from the back of the grid. He had earlier also picked up a grid penalty for a practice collision with Max Verstappen. The race itself has not yet aired on this flash.

Rugby League World Cup. Tonga beat Samoa twenty to eighteen in a tight final group match at Sydney's CommBank Stadium, with Addin Fonua-Blake scoring the winning try and Isaiya Katoa kicking the conversions and a penalty. The Kiwi Ferns beat Papua New Guinea to reach the semi-finals and now play Samoa this week.

Golf. New Zealand amateur Zack Swanwick lost his lead at the Asia Pacific Amateur Championship at Te Arai Links, triple bogeying late as Thailand's Fifa Laopakdee came through to win.

Football. Premier League leaders Arsenal beat Liverpool at Anfield, their first win there since 2012, to move three points clear at the top. In the A League, the Wellington Phoenix beat Newcastle Jets to make it three wins from three, guaranteeing them top of the table after round three.

Formula One context. Liam Lawson's disqualification compounds a difficult weekend after Saturday's practice collision with Verstappen, with both drivers blaming each other for debris left on track.

Coming up. The Mexican Grand Prix runs with Lawson starting from the back of the grid. The Kiwi Ferns play Samoa and the Kiwis play Fiji in Rugby League World Cup semi-finals this week. Election day is Saturday the seventh of November.

End of flash.
